taste.name: Serif Voice, Sans Utility
taste.trigger: When a medical brand had to sound like a person who listens, while still hosting pricing, nav and form UI.
taste.decision: Set every headline in Teodor 300 (a light serif) at 64/48/38px with negative tracking, over a single geometric sans for everything.
taste.reason: Patients arriving with chronic symptoms read a light serif as a considered voice; the sans (EuclidCircularB) is kept for the places they must act, so tone and function never share a typeface.
evidence: Teodor used on 24 elements, EuclidCircularB on 891

taste.name: Green-Black Instead of Black
taste.trigger: When choosing the ink and the inverse surface for text, nav, buttons and footer.
taste.decision: Used one deep teal-green #284849 as text, nav bar, primary button and dark section, and tinted every light neutral warm (#F8F6F2), over pure black on pure white.
taste.reason: A clinic that sells slow, root-cause care avoids the sterile white-and-black of urgent care; one ink for text and fill makes buttons and headlines feel like the same hand.
evidence: #284849 is text on 73 elements and 17.9% of background area
body text #333333 is the only neutral gray

taste.name: Pills Only for Actions
taste.trigger: When many elements could be rounded: buttons, inputs, cards, tables, modal.
taste.decision: Gave full-pill radius (9999px) to buttons, nav CTA and inputs only, and kept content panes at 12-16px or square, over rounding everything the same.
taste.reason: Pill shape reads as 'press here' before the label is read; flat-cornered pricing panels stay quiet so the price copy, not the box, carries the weight.
evidence: 40 elements at 9999px radius, 12 at 12px, 6 at 16px, 5 at 2px
pricing cards in screenshot at y=3000 are square-cornered on #F8F6F2

taste.name: Flat Surfaces, Color Blocks Do the Layering
taste.trigger: When separating hero, insurance, pricing, comparison and FAQ sections on a 10,429px page.
taste.decision: Separated sections by switching ground colors (#F8F6F2, #284849, #EBF2F0, #C1E5DB) and 80-120px padding, over card shadows, dividers or illustration.
taste.reason: Long clinical pages with prices and tables lose readers at every border; full-width color shifts mark 'new topic' without adding lines to parse. Restraint: no drop shadows on cards, no decorative gradients outside the photographic hero, no illustration.
evidence: only 2 non-ring shadows in the DOM (modal/popover)
